Let’s dive into Chapter 4: Breaking Unhealthy Patterns and Choosing Change.
You know, just noticing how ego states and life positions shape us—is only the first step. The real challenge? It’s breaking out of those automatic, sometimes self-defeating habits, and making new choices that actually serve us. That’s at the heart of personal growth—and it’s what helps us build healthier relationships.
Have you ever caught yourself stuck in the same old arguments, or feeling disappointed by familiar situations, even though you wish things could be different? It’s almost like your mind follows these well-worn trails—paths carved out by your early experiences, then deepened by years of habit.
So, what’s the key to real change? It’s self-awareness. When you can notice which ego state is running the show, or which life position is shaping your behavior, you’ve got a chance to hit pause—and actually make a conscious choice. That’s where your Adult state comes in.
Think of the Adult as the part of you that can step back, take a good look at what’s happening, and decide how to respond—instead of just reacting.
Here’s a real-world example. Imagine someone who grew up with really critical parents. Later on, whenever they hear feedback—even if it’s meant to be helpful—they might instantly slip into that defensive Child state. But, if they can spot that old pattern, their Adult self can step in and say, “Hey, this is different now. Feedback doesn’t have to be a threat—it can actually help me grow.”
Now, change isn’t about shutting down your Parent or Child states. They each have something valuable to offer—the Parent gives guidance and care, the Child brings creativity and emotion. The real goal is to let your Adult self bring them together, and help you pick the best response for the moment.
So, what can you actually do to break those unhealthy patterns? Here are a few practical tips:
- Start by tuning in to your emotional triggers. Ask yourself, “Which part of me is reacting right now?”
- Let your Adult state gather the facts, weigh your options, and make decisions based on where you are today—not where you were in the past.
- Try out new ways of responding in low-stress situations. Little by little, you’ll build up the confidence to use those skills even when the stakes feel higher.
And remember, you don’t have to go it alone. Getting feedback and encouragement from trusted friends, a counselor, or a support group can make a huge difference. Sometimes, just talking things through with someone who’s listening from their Adult state can help you see what’s really happening—and what new choices you have.
Most of all, be patient and gentle with yourself. Change doesn’t happen overnight—and it’s normal to hit a few bumps along the way. Every step you take toward more self-awareness and intentional action is a real win, even if it feels small.
By choosing to respond from your Adult state, and moving toward the “I’m OK – You’re OK” mindset, you’ll start to reshape your relationships—and your sense of self. The payoff? More freedom, more authenticity, and a deeper sense of satisfaction in every part of your life.
